speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light? Also, have you had any recent travel or exposure to ticks?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tic disorder and current use of haloperidol, I need to assess for signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. Are you experiencing any severe muscle rigidity, high blood pressure, or excessive sweating? I will also check your vital signs and muscle tone.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in the context of haloperidol use is highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will request laboratory tests to check for elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis to confirm this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase, Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis, combined with your clinical presentation of fever, rigidity, and altered mentation while on haloperidol, confirm my suspicion. I am ready to make a diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
